items.title: Microdelays disrupt online learning
items.author: Angela L. Duckworth
items.content: Analysing data from more than 80,000 students and aspiring coders, Mazar et al. show that microdelays, brief loading lags caused by slow internet connections, can impair online learning.

items.title: Recreational screen use and internalizing problems from preadolescence to young adulthood in a longitudinal twin cohort with co-twin comparison
items.author: Yi Lu
items.content: Using longitudinal twin data, this study finds that associations between youth recreational screen use and internalizing problems are substantially reduced within twin pairs, suggesting shared familial contributions to the observed association.

items.title: Contract incentives and behaviours of medical consultants in Ireland
items.author: Jiming Zhu
items.content: Using Irish inpatient data, this study finds that private practice within public hospitals, when paired with contractual ratio limits, can incentivize consultants to increase public admissions, but may reduce care quality for public patients.

items.title: Algorithm-assisted personalized risk communication to encourage flu vaccination in the USA: three randomized field trials
items.author: Christopher F. Chabris
items.content: Rosenbaum et al. show that targeted communications highlighting patients’ high-risk status increased influenza vaccination uptake. However, they did not find an additional effect of informing patients that a computer algorithm was used to identify their risk status.

items.title: Gendered motives for group formidability among children and adults
items.author: Lotte Thomsen
items.content: Fonn et al. find that boys but not girls prefer larger groups by age three, and these preferences predict support for group-based hierarchy among adults. This suggests that gendered motives for intergroup formidability are rooted in earliest childhood.

items.title: Intrinsic rewards guide visual resource allocation via reinforcement learning
items.author: Paul M. Bays
items.content: Tangible rewards are known to sharpen visual processing of associated objects. Tomić et al. show that an internal sense of confidence—acting as an intrinsic reward—similarly biases attention, revealing how the brain prioritizes limited resources.

items.title: Selfish and prosocial individuals both distort their actions’ impact, but selfish distortions can be more contagious
items.author: Jörg Gross
items.content: In this study, Vollberg and Gross show that both selfish and prosocial individuals exaggerate the social benefits of their choices, with selfish-serving distortions proving to be socially contagious.

items.title: Introducing AI to an online petition platform changed outputs but not outcomes
items.author: Mor Naaman
items.content: Corpus et al. examine how the introduction of an AI writing tool impacted Change.org petitions, finding that it increased petition homogeneity but did not improve petition outcomes.
